questions.q: Lab settings: $P = \mathcal{N}(0, 1^2)$ and $Q = \mathcal{N}(1, 1^2)$. Using the closed form, what is $D_{KL}(P \parallel Q)$?
questions.explain: $\ln(\sigma_Q/\sigma_P) = 0$ and $\frac{\sigma_P^2 + (\mu_P - \mu_Q)^2}{2\sigma_Q^2} - \frac12 = \frac{1 + 1}{2} - \frac12 = 0.5$ nats. Dividing by $\ln 2$ converts to bits: $\approx 0.721$. $0.5$ forgets the unit conversion.

questions.q: With $P = \mathcal{N}(0, 1^2)$ and a wider $Q = \mathcal{N}(0, 2^2)$, forward KL is $\approx 0.46$ bits but reverse KL $D_{KL}(Q \parallel P) \approx 1.16$ bits. What does this show?
options: One of the two numbers must be a rounding error
Reverse KL is always exactly 2.5 times forward KL
KL divergence can be negative when the model is too wide
KL divergence is asymmetric, so it is not a true distance metric
questions.explain: $D_{KL}(P \parallel Q) \neq D_{KL}(Q \parallel P)$ in general. Both values are still $\ge 0$ (Gibbs' inequality); there is no fixed ratio between them.

questions.q: $P$ has two well-separated modes. Which behavior does minimizing **reverse** KL $D_{KL}(Q \parallel P)$ tend to produce in a single-mode model $Q$?
options: Mean-seeking: $Q$ stretches to cover both modes
$Q$ becomes uniform over the whole line
Mode-seeking: $Q$ locks onto one mode and fits it tightly
$Q$ places most mass in the empty gap between the modes
questions.explain: Reverse KL heavily penalizes $Q$ for putting mass where $P \approx 0$ (zero-forcing), so $Q$ concentrates on one mode. Covering every mode is the forward-KL (zero-avoiding, mean-seeking) behavior.

questions.q: Discrete example: $P = [0.5,\ 0.5]$, $Q = [0.25,\ 0.75]$. What is $D_{KL}(P \parallel Q) = \sum_x P(x)\log_2\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}$?
questions.explain: $0.5\log_2(0.5/0.25) + 0.5\log_2(0.5/0.75) = 0.5 \cdot 1 + 0.5 \cdot (-0.585) \approx 0.208$ bits. One term is negative, but the total is never below $0$; it is $0$ only if $P = Q$.
